Area.evidence_source: Difficulty in communicating (eg, minimizing symptoms and needs) in response to a number of interrelated stressors involving loss of personal control, rejection and failure to achieve expected work or family goals was commonly reported. Externalizing (eg, irritability, anger, aggression, alcohol abuse, or increasing workload), somatic (eg, hypersomnia or insomnia, fatigue), painful somatic/physical conditions (back pain, tinnitus, and headaches) were more commonly reported than internalizing (eg, ruminating, withdrawal, anxiety, and depression) symptoms. (F6) Negative cognitive processes were reflected within the narratives (ie, guilt, shame and regret, anger with frustration, jealousy, pessimism, paranoia, and cognitive distortion or rigidity). Internalizing disorders such as depression and anxiety (eg, isolation, withdrawal, rumination, and negative bias), externalized coping (ie, verbal/physical aggression, increased alcohol/cannabis consumption ("self-medicating"), low engagement in health care (ie, priority of work over health, lack of mental health knowledge, minimization of pain and severity/seriousness of illness, and low treatment adherence); and suicidality (despair, hopelessness, worthlessness, and perceived burdensomeness) were also reported. A small number of farmers experienced long-term mental health disorders since early adulthood, with frequent hospitalization, suicide exposure and communication of intent to health professionals reported.
